title: I-27 Numbering Act of 2023
official_summary:
I–27 Numbering Act of 2023

This bill designates the future interstate highway system portions of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor within the states of Texas and New Mexico as Interstate Route I–27.

In Texas, from Sterling City to Lamesa, U.S. Route 87 is designated as Interstate Route I–27E and Texas Routes 158 and 349 via I–20 are designated as Interstate Route I–27W. The bill also excludes one portion of the Texas and New Mexico corridor; U.S. Route 287 from Dumas, Texas to the border between Texas and Oklahoma is designated as Interstate Route I–127N.

summary.headline: Law sets the interstate route numbers for future highway segments of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor in Texas and New Mexico.
summary.what_it_does: This law names the future interstate highway parts of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor in Texas and New Mexico as Interstate 27 (I-27). Between Sterling City and Lamesa, Texas, the route splits in two: U.S. Route 87 becomes I-27E, and Texas Routes 158 and 349 (using I-20) become I-27W. U.S. Route 287 from Dumas, Texas, to the Oklahoma border is numbered separately as I-127N. The summary describes only route numbering, not new funding or construction.

who_it_affects.group: Drivers and truckers using highways in West Texas, the Texas Panhandle, and eastern New Mexico
who_it_affects.how: Certain roads they use will carry I-27, I-27E, I-27W, or I-127N interstate numbers once those sections become part of the interstate system.

who_it_affects.group: Texas and New Mexico state transportation agencies
who_it_affects.how: They will use these assigned numbers for the corridor's future interstate segments, such as on signs and maps.

who_it_affects.group: Communities along the corridor, including Sterling City, Lamesa, and Dumas, Texas
who_it_affects.how: Highways through or near these towns are assigned specific interstate route numbers.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted March 22, 2024; the summary gives no separate start date.
